frontier.hypothesis: The whole remaining residual reduces to getting the 640 constant allocated a register that no earlier constant used, in pure C — i.e. defeating sched1's sink of its set so its live range survives into local-alloc.
frontier.mechanism: The pin diagnostic proves the register is what frees BOTH the sh 0x10 store's slot and the RGB block's field order; a 2-insn live range is what makes local-alloc reuse $v0. Anything that keeps the 640 pseudo live from the block head to its late uses forces a second register, and sched1's sink is what prevents that. Note the pinned build still has one residual (li 640 after li 128 rather than ahead of li 240), so the register may be necessary-but-not-sufficient — expect a second, smaller lever behind it.
frontier.next_probe: Look for a pure-C shape whose 640 value has a use the scheduler cannot sink past: e.g. the value flowing through a variable that is ALSO used by an insn target emits early, a value obtained by a non-constant-foldable expression that still assembles to a single addiu-from-zero, or the two 640 stores written as a chained assignment (sp[16] = sp[8] = 640) so the single pseudo has two dependent stores. Score each with sandbox --disable all and, for anything at 2 or below, confirm the register with tmp/grind/func_8003553C/s3/rtl.sh + grep of base.i.greg. Do NOT re-try constant holders in their plain spelling, the OT-load spellings, MEM_IN_STRUCT_P, or other-constant live-range extenders — all measured dead.

frontier.hypothesis: decomp-permuter from the score-2 base can find the register-lifetime shape that hand enumeration cannot express.
frontier.mechanism: The search target is no longer statement order (saturated at 2 over ~45 orderings) but a register-lifetime shape — exactly what the permuter's temp introduction / expression re-association / variable-reuse mutations explore, and a base score of 2 gives a clean gradient.
frontier.next_probe: Build a clean single-function target.o from asm/funcs/func_8003553C.s + tools/decomp-permuter/prelude.inc (function at offset 0, drop the .set gp=64 line) per .claude/rules/difficult-is-not-impossible.md section 3; seed base.c from memory/grind/func_8003553C/candidate.c; run a fresh-seed campaign with tools/permuter_campaign.py, waiting for it IN-TURN via `permuter_campaign.py wait --dir <ws>` and harvesting + `--stop`ing before writing the outcome. Run import.py from a subdirectory, not the repo root (a root-level nonmatchings/ breaks the driver's scope check). Vet any closing form against the cheat catalog before banking it.

frontier.hypothesis: A matched sibling in the tree already contains the C spelling that materializes a constant into a SECOND register at a block head with only late uses (target's li $v1,K shape).
frontier.mechanism: If any COMPLETED function's asm shows `addiu $vN,$zero,K` at a block head with its first use several insns later, its C source is direct evidence of a spelling that survives sched1's sink — the exact thing this function needs, obtained by reading rather than guessing.
frontier.next_probe: Grep asm/funcs/*.s (or the objdump of build/) for a block-head `addiu $v1,$zero,<imm>` whose first consumer is >=4 insns later inside functions NOT in engine/queue.json (i.e. already matched), then read the corresponding C body (Grep to locate, Read with offset/limit — never whole src files). Compare its constant's live-range shape with ours and transplant the spelling.
